label: input p late in the original phase, strongest when the sequence starts with n
explanation: Very sparse feature (about 0.015% of steps). 98% of activation mass is in the original phase and 87% of it falls on input token p at positions 4-8, peaking at position 5-6. It never fires before position 3 and never fires in the copy phase. A small amount (2%) fires on <DEL> when the first output is n. Magnitude depends strongly on history: the sequence starting with n (first_tok n, 21x lift, 78% of mass) and earlier r or e (especially r just before p) both raise it. All of the top examples are n ... r/e ... p. Input p alone gives recall 0.81 but precision 0.02, because most late p inputs stay silent. Adding first token == n brings precision up to 0.35 and recall down to 0.50 (dev F1 0.41, mass recall 0.66). Requiring earlier r/e/k/a/o only reaches F1 0.45. The exact conjunction of history that gates it is not fully captured, and it also has weak activations on late p in sequences that do not start with n.

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 40 cues. Raise it: orig0=n (+6.56), phase=0 & in_tok=p (+3.72), recall_idx=-1 & in_tok=p (+3.72), prev_tok=r (+3.41), orig1=k (+3.20), orig0=w (+2.45). Lower it: correct=1 (-6.62), prev3_tok=- (-3.14), t=3 (-2.78), phase=2 (-2.38).
